examples.label: OSCP Ch17 — find writable directories as current user

notes: World-writable files owned/run by root are the raw material for cron, wildcard, and logrotate attacks. Separate the directory search from the file search - a writable dir lets you swap files even if you can't edit them. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 17 (Linux Privilege Escalation).

recommended.note: Feed a writable root-run script into a cron abuse.
Writable dir under a tar-* cron -> checkpoint abuse.

name: Enumeration - World-Writable Files and Directories
description: World-writable files (especially root-run scripts/cron targets) and directories are prime escalation vectors. Prunes /proc to reduce noise.

defense.why_it_works: World-writable files and directories can be modified by any user on the system. If a world-writable file is executed by a privileged process (cron job, startup script, systemd unit), modifying it allows injecting commands that run with elevated privileges.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access as any user. World-writable files referenced by privileged processes.
defense.impact: Identifies injection points for privilege escalation: writable cron scripts, writable files in $PATH, writable Python/library files, writable config files loaded by privileged services.
defense.detection: Auditd: find command with -perm -o+w searching filesystem. Unusual writes to system directories. File integrity monitoring (AIDE, Tripwire) detecting permission changes.
defense.artifacts: Auditd: find -perm -o+w executed | File integrity alert on world-writable file creation
defense.prevention: Regularly audit world-writable files: find / -not /proc -type f -perm -o+w 2>/dev/null. Remove world-write permission where not necessary. Use umask 022 or 027 as default. Apply sticky bit to world-writable directories (/tmp, /var/tmp). Avoid creating world-writable files in system directories.
defense.misconfiguration: System files or scripts referenced by cron/systemd are world-writable, allowing any local user to inject malicious code executed with root privileges.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# World-writable script run by root cron
-rwxrwxrwx 1 root root /usr/local/bin/cleanup.sh

# World-writable /tmp without sticky bit
drwxrwxrwx 1 root root /tmp
defense.secure_config:
# Fix world-writable permissions
find / -not /proc -type f -perm -o+w 2>/dev/null | xargs chmod o-w

# Apply sticky bit to shared directories
chmod +t /tmp /var/tmp

# Set secure umask
echo 'umask 027' >> /etc/profile
